task: Quality authority reconciliation for dependency manifests before the source-map-js security remediation.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The dependency security fix cannot be planned safely while package.json and package-lock.json are semantically unowned by the canonical domain registry. This transaction repairs only that architecture classification before any dependency edit.

acceptanceCriteria: package.json and package-lock.json classify as DOMAIN-RELEASE with release-infrastructure authority.
The change is limited to canonical domain classification plus deterministic Atlas regression.
Dependency package contents are not edited in this transaction.
Existing DOMAIN-QUALITY and other domain classifications remain unchanged.
invariants: Dependency manifests describe the install/release contract but do not become business-domain truth.
The classifier uses exact root manifest paths rather than a broad JSON glob.
No dependency version is changed before this Plan Before Code transaction passes.

failureModes: The dependency security edit is attempted while package manifests remain Atlas-unresolved.
A broad *.json release path steals ownership from unrelated canonical JSON knowledge.
Only package.json is classified and package-lock.json remains unresolved.
The authority registry is changed without a classifier regression.
The security version change is mixed into this precondition transaction before Plan Before Code validates the authority model.
Release authority is confused with runtime package behavior authority.
The change weakens unresolved-scope checks instead of classifying the real dependency manifests.
edgeCases: Both package.json and package-lock.json are repository-root exact paths.
Nested package manifests, if introduced later, are not silently claimed by this exact-path rule.

alternatives.summary: Add an exception so package files can bypass Atlas resolution.
alternatives.reason: That would weaken the canonical unresolved-scope guard.

alternatives.summary: Treat dependency manifests as neutral files.
alternatives.reason: Dependency changes carry release/security risk and must remain governed.

alternatives.summary: Assign only root package.json and package-lock.json to DOMAIN-RELEASE.
alternatives.reason: Dependency manifests are release/install contracts and this preserves exact ownership without broad classification.

specialistReviews.finding: Dependency manifests currently have a release-risk subsystem but no canonical domain path.
specialistReviews.resolution: Add exact root manifest paths to DOMAIN-RELEASE.

specialistReviews.finding: Marking package files neutral would make a security-relevant dependency edit invisible to architecture closure.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep dependency-contract risk classification and give manifests explicit release-domain ownership.

specialistReviews.finding: The subsequent source-map-js patch needs package manifests to be dependency-closed and Atlas-resolved.
specialistReviews.resolution: This precondition transaction establishes release ownership before the security scope expands.

challenge.finding: Without canonical domain ownership it blocks as unresolved.
Lockfile must be governed identically to its manifest.
It can steal unrelated knowledge/config authority.

challenge.scenario: The security version is edited now.
challenge.finding: That would begin the dependency implementation before its semantic authority is valid.
challenge.resolution: Dependency contents stay read-only until the next reviewed plan expansion.

challenge.finding: Future unknown dependency files could pass silently.

challenge.scenario: The release domain is mistaken for package runtime ownership.
challenge.finding: Business/runtime code could inherit release truth incorrectly.
challenge.resolution: Only manifest paths are classified; package behavior remains external dependency behavior.

challenge.finding: A future domain registry edit could silently unclassify dependency manifests.
challenge.resolution: Add deterministic classifyAtlasPath assertions for both files.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code on this exact plan-only head.
Add only exact package.json/package-lock.json canonical paths to DOMAIN-RELEASE.
Add deterministic Atlas regression for release-domain classification.
Run Edit-Time and full Known Failure Replay.
Only after this coherent batch passes, regenerate the plan to include the dependency security edit.

requirements.requirement: Root dependency manifests have canonical DOMAIN-RELEASE ownership before security-sensitive dependency edits are allowed.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: package.json and package-lock.json must not remain semantically unclassified.
The fix must not broadly classify unrelated JSON files as release authority.

notes: Precondition for the source-map-js security remediation. The security audit currently fails on source-map-js 1.2.1, but dependency contents remain read-only until root package manifests have canonical DOMAIN-RELEASE ownership. This transaction intentionally does not weaken security-audit or Plan Before Code.
